function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick “cheat‑sheet” you can use to find a short (≤ 120 min) movie that’s still within walking distance of Times Square:

| Theater | Approx. distance from Times Square | How to filter by runtime |
|---------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** (Broadway & W 34th St) | ~0.3 mi (≈ 5 min walk) | On the AMC website or Fandango, use the “Runtime” filter (e.g., “Under 2 hrs”). |
| **Regal Times Square** (Broadway & W 34th St) | ~0.2 mi (≈ 4 min walk) | On Regal’s site or Fandango, filter by “Duration” → “< 120 min”. |
| **AMC Lexington Center** (Lexington Ave & W 34th St) | ~0.4 mi (≈ 7 min walk) | Same as above. |
| **Regal Times Square 2** (Broadway & W 34th St) | ~0.2 mi | Same as above. |
| **AMC Times Square** (Broadway & W 34th St) | ~0.2 mi | Same as above. |

> **Tip:** All of these theaters are within a 10‑minute walk of Times Square, so you can easily hop out of the subway, grab a coffee, and head straight to the screen.

---

### How to find a movie ≤ 2 hrs

1. **Pick a theater** (any of the ones above).  
2. **Go to Fandango** (or the theater’s own site).  
   * Example: <https://www.fandango.com/nyc-theaters/amc-empire-25-12345>  
3. **Use the “Runtime” filter** (most sites call it “Duration” or “Length”).  
   * Choose “Under 2 hrs” or set a custom range (e.g., 90–120 min).  
4. **Browse the list** – you’ll see all movies currently playing that meet the length requirement.  
5. **Book a seat** – Fandango will let you pick a showtime that fits your schedule.

---

### Sample movies that are usually ≤ 2 hrs (check the current listings)

| Movie | Runtime | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| *The Grand Budapest Hotel* | 1 h 39 min | Classic Wes Anderson, great for a quick watch. |
| *The Social Network* | 1 h 49 min | David Fincher, fast‑paced drama. |
| *The Imitation Game* | 1 h 58 min | Historical thriller, under 2 hrs. |
| *The King's Speech* | 1 h 45 min | Oscar‑winning biopic. |
| *The Theory of Everything* | 1 h 55 min | Biographical drama about Stephen Hawking. |
| *The Big Short* | 1 h 57 min | Financial drama, under 2 hrs. |
| *The Last Duel* | 2 h 12 min | Slightly over 2 hrs – keep an eye on the exact runtime. |
| *The Irishman* | 3 h 29 min | Too long – skip if you’re strict about the 2‑hr limit. |

> **Note:** Runtime can vary slightly between releases (theatrical cut vs. extended cut). Always double‑check the runtime shown on the ticketing site before booking.

---

### Quick navigation

If you’re already in Times Square and want to walk to a theater:

| Destination | Walking time (approx.) | Directions |
|-------------|------------------------|------------|
| AMC Empire 25 | 5 min | Walk south on Broadway, turn left onto W 34th St, then right onto Lexington Ave. |
| Regal Times Square | 4 min | Walk east on Broadway, turn left onto W 34th St, then right onto 7th Ave. |
| AMC Lexington Center | 7 min | Walk south on Broadway, turn left onto W 34th St, then right onto Lexington Ave. |

> **Pro tip:** Use Google Maps or Apple Maps to get real‑time walking directions and estimated times. Just type “AMC Empire 25” or “Regal Times Square” into the search bar.

---

### Final checklist

1. **Choose a theater** (any of the ones listed).  
2. **Open Fandango** (or the theater’s site).  
3. **Filter by runtime** (≤ 120 min).  
4. **Select a showtime** that works for you.  
5. **Book tickets** and enjoy a quick, quality movie experience within walking distance of Times Square!

Happy watching!
